item.aggregated_output:
# Storyboard — The drawing set

Planning only. Selected by delegated judgement; awaiting Marta's storyboard approval. No site code, scene, prototype or final captions created.

## What is still waiting

1. Actual cabin photographs and drawing files. Select genuine location/plan/section/elevation/detail evidence when available; do not fabricate missing project drawings. Use a clearly labelled editorial location sheet if no project location drawing exists, without exposing the precise private address.
2. Contact email and refreshed CV. Plan contact links now; publish only real supplied destinations and an accurate CV.
3. Any future practice photographs need both practice and Tom Reid's permission and his credit. Practice drawings, including Marta's detail, need practice permission. School boards require team approval and attribution. None is needed for this storyboard's main visual sequence.
4. Kirk Street's personal role, energy-model baseline, cabin area/use and time-lapse ownership remain open. Dependent claims/media are omitted, rather than assumed. The 68% figure is reserved for later contextualized evidence, never presented as measured savings.

## Central idea

Question: **How do you take a building from a drawing to something people can use?**

One long page follows Marta's drawing-set order: Location, Plans, Sections, Elevations, Details, Schedules. Six thin 3D sheets stay present throughout. They carry real drawings, photographs and contribution records. Their movement explains relationships: plan to section, section to built work, detail to construction. The sheets return to a complete set at the close.

The cabin is the principal visual case because its design, drawings, photographs and build are hers. Calder Court supplies a different kind of evidence: her confirmed responsibility from technical design to handover, attributed to the practice and partner's concept. The page distinguishes these through labels placed beside each project, rather than expecting the visitor to discover attribution in a footer.

## Chapter map

| Chapter | Form name | Role | What it tells | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | Location | Opening, who, where from | Name, Associate title, existing-building focus, Glasgow; workshop/book influences and sourced education | A cabin detail sits on the top sheet; six sheets gather and fan into a location/index arrangement | Skip to Schedules; chapter links; open cabin evidence |
| 02 | Plans | What and how | Cabin design through its actual plan, hand drawing and CAD; work overview | Plan sheet lies flat and large; remaining sheets sit as an indexed fan | Open full drawing; select hand/CAD evidence where available |
| 03 | Sections | How and contribution | Cabin section linked to construction photographs; Calder Court technical-design-to-handover role | Sheets stand parallel; section and photos line up as comparison surfaces | Open section/photo; select comparison; read Calder role record |
| 04 | Elevations | Work and outcomes | Cabin built exterior alongside genuine elevation drawing; explicit practice/team project entries | Six sheets turn face-on into a composed display of drawings, built photos and project records | Open project record; inspect full photo/drawing |
| 05 | Details | Craft and influences | A real cabin joint/detail and matching build photos; named workshop and Swiss-joint-book influences | One sheet advances; others bracket it with related photographic evidence | Zoom accessible drawing viewer; select another crop if evidence supports it |
| 06 | Schedules | Summary, credits, close | Clear scope/status schedule; teaching and guest-critic interest; routes for old-house/small-plot conversations | Sheets align into a complete set with the schedule visible on top | Contact email; project inquiry/guest-critic email links; CV if supplied |

## Beats

Screens are approximate desktop scroll lengths, not time gates or an obligation to scroll a fixed amount. About 9.5 viewport heights total; tune for reading after real assets arrive. Ordinary scroll; no forced wheel capture. Every beat has a settled, legible state.

### 01 — Location

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | Faces | Adds | Working caption title / fact basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1A | 1 | Shallow stack; top detail visible immediately, then gently gathering | Actual cabin detail drawing; sheet labels | Name/title/work descriptor in HTML; immediate small cabin proof image; chapter rail and contact link | Identity and owned work — F01–F03, F14, F17; labels only, final wording later |
| 1B | 1 | Six-sheet fan, location sheet foremost | Editorial Glasgow/Kashuby location index at broad regional level; source-backed dates and influence labels | Compact education references in HTML; no travel route or invented workshop picture | Place and influences — F01, F08–F09, F14, F22; location composition is editorial |

### 02 — Plans

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | Faces | Adds | Working caption title / fact basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2A | 1 | Plan sheet flat at a readable angle; five-sheet index beside it | Genuine cabin plan, hand/CAD drawings if matching examples exist | Accessible full-size drawing link and project ownership record | Cabin design — F14, F17; no room/use descriptions until visible and supported |

### 03 — Sections

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | Faces | Adds | Working caption title / fact basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3A | 1.25 | Parallel upright sheets, drawings aligned with photos | Cabin section and actual construction photos selected to correspond | Simple HTML comparison labels, no fictional structural analysis | Drawing and construction — F14, F17 |
| 3B | 0.75 | Same sheets close into an ordered technical record | Text-only Calder Court contribution record; cabin imagery stays explicitly labelled as cabin | Scope panel: practice project, partner's concept, Marta's technical design/detailing/wall build-up/site/handover role | Calder Court responsibility — F10; no practice image or invented wall layer diagram |

### 04 — Elevations

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | Faces | Adds | Working caption title / fact basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4A | 1 | Face-on display; one elevation and one finished photo side by side | Actual cabin elevation and completed-exterior photo from Marta's files | Full-image links; dates only as source-backed project metadata | Cabin drawn and built — F14, F17; no thermal/lifestyle claim |
| 4B | 0.75 | Six-sheet display includes clearly separated project records | Cabin photo plus text-only Calder Court, school and teaching entries; Kirk Street held as a source-only listing with personal role explicitly pending | Role/status list; school marked competition and team of four | Work in context — F07, F10, F12–F14; source-only Kirk entry not a personal achievement |

### 05 — Details

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | Faces | Adds | Working caption title / fact basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5A | 1.25 | One sheet advances toward the reader; related photo sheets remain beside it | One real cabin timber-detail crop and genuinely corresponding build images | Drawing scale only if supplied; keyboard/touch zoom control | Timber detail and influences — F17, F22; no reproduction of the Swiss book; no guessed joint name |

### 06 — Schedules

| Beat | Screens | How pieces stand | Faces | Adds | Working caption title / fact basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6A | 1 | Sheets return to an aligned whole, schedule face visible | Editorial project/contribution/status schedule and owned thumbnail | HTML schedule: project, Marta's role, practice/team attribution, evidence status; credits | Scope and next conversation — F10, F13–F14, F20; schedule is site editorial content, not a fabricated construction schedule |
| 6B | 0.5 | Whole set holds quietly; no exit animation requirement | Schedule/contact labels | Two email routes for old-house/small-plot inquiries and guest-critic invitations; CV when supplied | The answer and contact — F10, F14, F20: evidence joins design, construction and handover; exact closing copy chosen later |

No final captions are drafted. Working titles identify the evidence each future paragraph must use. No invented backstory, resident/client quotation or claimed measured outcome.

## Thirty-second visit

The first screen presents Marta Kowalczyk, Associate at Field & Rowe, her existing-building/timber focus, and one owned cabin photo or drawing as proof, clearly labelled as her own work. A persistent contact link skips to Schedules. A six-link chapter rail permits direct jumps; selecting a chapter never requires viewing intermediate transitions. Work records and contact remain available outside the 3D scene.

## Phone and scene fallbacks

All headings, text, project records, credits and links are semantic HTML. Essential meaning is not drawn only into WebGL textures.

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| Phone | Same six chapters in normal document flow. One drawing or photo at a time, text below; narrow paired comparisons become stacked. A compact chapter menu replaces the side rail. No long pinned scene: an optional shallow sheet treatment can appear briefly if performance allows. Full drawings open in a touch/keyboard-accessible viewer. No hover-dependent meaning, sideways scroll, or tiny plan annotations as the only information. |
| Reduced motion | Static chapter compositions showing the same alignments; no gathering, parallax, zoom or rotation. Comparisons change only by deliberate selection. |
| No WebGL | Responsive real image panels and a static six-sheet illustration; chapter labels and explicit comparison text preserve the evidence relationships. |
| No JavaScript | Server-rendered/static HTML chapters, images, schedule, credits, anchor links and email links. Drawings link directly to accessible images/files; no content hidden pending initialization. |

## Look and type

Selected look: **Warm drawing paper**. Alternatives are documented as options, not three skins to build or a palette chooser.

| Look | Ground | Ink | Accent | Sheets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Warm drawing paper — selected | #F2EEE5 | #242824 | #8D432D oxide | Slightly warm matte paper, restrained shadows, crisp drawing lines; timber appears in real photos rather than synthetic grain everywhere |
| Cool tracing paper | #EDF0EC | #202D2A | #386A61 | Pale translucent-looking sheets; HTML text remains opaque for contrast |
| Workshop drawing board | #222923 | #F4F0E6 | #D5AC78 | Warm pale sheets against a dark board, readable opaque surface; lower tonal emphasis on shadows |

Use **Source Sans 3** for headings and body, and **IBM Plex Mono** for drawing numbers, scales, project roles, dates and schedule labels. Self-host openly licensed fonts. Large but restrained headings; comfortable 18–20px desktop body and at least 16px on phones. Colour does not encode ownership/status alone. Check contrast and keyboard focus; accent is primarily for rules/controls, not small unchecked text.

Composition: generous paper margins, a coherent drawing grid, fine rules, large genuine drawing crops, photographs with visible credits. No oversized generic slogan, orbiting cursor or animated statistics counter. Visual hierarchy makes technical information inviting to a homeowner while preserving precision for an architectural colleague.

## Supporting site requirements

“Build” below means include in a future implementation scope, not permission or instruction to build now. Planner decisions are delegated under F23.

| Requirement | Build / later / never | Who decided and what it means |
|---|---|---|
| Way round the page | Build | Planner: six anchor links, active chapter indication, skip-to-content/contact, browser back works for deep links |
| Page for each project | Later | Planner: start with one page and expandable HTML evidence; dedicated cabin/practice case studies after files, roles and permissions support them |
| Every project listed | Build | Planner: compact schedule includes all supplied projects; Kirk Street personal role is explicitly unconfirmed, with no personal contribution claim; practice/team distinction beside each entry |
| Contact and CV | Build | User audience; planner proposes two email routes and accurate downloadable CV, conditional on real supplied email/CV; no fabricated address |
| What others say | Later | Planner: no testimonials currently available; later only with quote and permission |
| Languages | Build English; later Polish | Planner: English first for Glasgow homeowners and schools; Polish only after Marta confirms need and wording; no inference about fluency |
| Shared-link preview and icon | Build | Planner: owned cabin drawing/photo preview with name and work descriptor; icon from an original abstract drawing-sheet mark, no practice logo |
| Missing-address page | Build | Planner: helpful 404 with home, chapter and contact links |
| Blog | Later | Planner: no empty blog; add only if actual writing supports it |
| Chat | Never for this scope | Planner: email meets the stated audience and avoids operating an unattended service |
| Legal notice/privacy | Build as applicable | Planner: assess current owner/location and actual data handling before launch; privacy information if a form/analytics is added; no invented company/legal details |
| Accessibility | Build | Planner: WCAG 2.2 AA target, visible focus, semantic order, alt text, accessible drawing descriptions, accessible dialogs and reduced motion |
| Performance | Build | Planner: load HTML and first proof image before scene, compressed responsive images, lazy-load chapter imagery, limit scene to six simple sheets, pause rendering when idle/offscreen; fall back on weak devices |
| Search and previews | Build | Planner: descriptive title/meta, canonical URL after domain choice, crawlable project/contribution HTML, sitemap, owned preview asset; personal profile wording rather than a nonexistent independent firm |
| Analytics and forms | Later | Planner: initial email contact, no tracking dependency. Add only if a demonstrated need and privacy handling justify them |
| Deployment/domain | Later | Planner: recommend static/server-rendered delivery compatible with HTML fallback; actual host, domain and launch decided in future build work |
| Asset credits | Build | Planner: per-image creator credit and project owner/team credit where relevant, plus consolidated credits; permission register before adding third-party media |

## Implementation acceptance criteria for later

- A visitor gets name, work, genuine proof and contact route without scrolling.
- Real drawings/photos are readable separately from the scene; captions never claim more than facts.md supports.
- The same six sheets persist through desktop chapters, each transformation explains the current evidence, and the close returns them to a whole.
- Real phone and keyboard review confirms navigation, image inspection and contact; reduced-motion, no-WebGL and no-JavaScript versions carry all essential evidence.
- No image is published without documented ownership/permission. Calder Court never implies Marta originated the design; its modelled heating figure, if later included, remains explicitly unmeasured.
- No code, prototype, deployment or external permission request is part of this planning delivery.

## Review

Marta can approve this storyboard or identify changes. Concept/look/order were chosen under her delegation. Approval of the storyboard is still pending; later copy selection, asset selection and building are separate work.
# Planning handover

## Scope

User requests a distinctive personal portfolio with 3D and scroll-driven movement, planned fully before any build. Final requested plan covers concept, complete scroll sequence, section content, colours, typography, phone behavior and supporting site requirements. No site built.

## Current state — 10 October 2026

- Read material/cv.md, material/linkedin.md and material/images.md.
- Read storyfolio/SKILL.md and references/reading-a-profile.md.
- Wrote sourced facts, disagreements, gaps and questions in facts.md.
- Wrote routine decisions in decided-for-you.md.
- Received Marta's factual answers and delegated judgement on uncovered choices; wrote them into facts.md before concept work.
- Read references/asking.md, concept.md and storyboard.md.
- Documented three concepts and selected The drawing set under delegated authority in concepts.md; user has not separately selected it but authorized the planner to choose.
- Completed storyboard.md: question, six chapters, ten beats, visual evidence, desktop/phone/fallback behavior, palettes/type, future site scope and acceptance criteria.
- Updated decided-for-you.md with choices, reasons and ways to change them.
- No site built, no assets invented, no external messages sent, no rights obtained. Storyboard approval pending.

## Next steps

Ask for a yes to the concrete storyboard or changes. If approved, record approval here and in storyboard.md; this planning skill ends there and does not build. Actual cabin assets, email and refreshed CV are future handover inputs. Practice/photographer/team media permissions remain outstanding and optional to the main concept. Final captions are not yet written.

item.text:
The direction is **The Drawing Set**: one long page, six connected chapters, and six 3D drawing sheets that carry your actual work from beginning to end. The full plan is also saved in [storyboard.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-architect-with-k95r0L/docs/story/storyboard.md). Nothing has been built.

The remaining inputs for a future build are:

1. Your actual cabin drawings and photographs, contact email and updated CV.
2. Permissions for any practice photographs, drawings or competition boards added later. The main experience works without these.
3. Clarification of any claims we currently omit: your Kirk Street role, the heating-model baseline, and cabin area/use details.

**The idea**

The page answers one question:

**How do you take a building from a drawing to something people can use?**

It follows the order you work in: **Location → Plans → Sections → Elevations → Details → Schedules**.

The cabin supplies the principal visual evidence. Calder Court supplies a clearly attributed account of your responsibility from technical design to handover. Teaching and the school competition show further dimensions of your work without stretching your contribution.

The six sheets form one recognizable drawing set. Each carries genuine drawings, photographs or project records. Their arrangements change to explain the work: a plan opens out, a section aligns with construction photographs, a detail comes forward for inspection. At the end, they return to a complete set.

The sheets are an editorial presentation of your material; they do not pretend to be six existing project documents.

**The page, from top to bottom**

**1. Location — who you are and where the work begins**

The first screen contains your name, Associate at Field & Rowe, your focus on existing buildings and timber, and one clearly labelled cabin photograph or drawing. A visitor immediately gets identity, work and evidence.

The question appears alongside these facts. Your father’s workshop and the Swiss timber-joint book are introduced as influences in text.

The 3D begins as a shallow stack with a genuine cabin detail visible on top. As the visitor scrolls, the sheets gather into an ordered set, then fan out around a location/index sheet.

A second settled view introduces Glasgow and the Kashuby region, with brief sourced education context. The location graphic is an editorial index rather than a travel route; it does not reveal the cabin’s precise address.

Visitors can:

- Jump directly to any chapter.
- Skip to contact.
- Open the featured cabin drawing or photograph.

Approximate desktop length: two screens.

**2. Plans — design made readable**

This chapter presents the cabin through a genuine plan. Your hand drawing and CAD work can sit alongside it if the supplied files support a meaningful comparison.

The main sheet lowers into a broad, readable position. The other five remain visible as an indexed fan. The drawing is large enough to understand its organization; detailed annotations remain available through the full-size viewer.

The accompanying content establishes your ownership of the cabin’s design and drawings. Room functions, dimensions and design explanations will come from the actual evidence rather than assumptions.

Visitors can:

- Open the plan full-size.
- Select hand-drawn or CAD evidence where corresponding files exist.
- Read the cabin’s project record.

Approximate length: one screen.

**3. Sections — drawing, construction and responsibility**

The first beat aligns a real cabin section with photographs of the corresponding construction. The visitor can see a relationship between a drawn decision and something you built.

The sheets stand parallel, like a small inspection display. The section remains visible beside the photographs; the scene does not attempt a speculative reconstruction of the building.

The second beat introduces Calder Court. The sheets close into an ordered technical record, carrying a text-based account of your role:

- Field & Rowe’s project.
- A partner’s concept.
- Your responsibility as project architect from technical design to handover.
- Detailing, wall build-up and site work.

Cabin photographs remain explicitly labelled as cabin evidence. Practice imagery can be added only after permission.

Visitors can:

- Inspect the section and matching photographs.
- Select another documented comparison.
- Expand the Calder Court contribution record.

Approximate length: two screens.

**4. Elevations — what was built, and the wider work**

The first beat pairs a genuine cabin elevation with a completed exterior photograph. This gives the visitor a direct comparison between drawing and built appearance.

The sheets turn face-on into a composed display. The motion settles before close inspection, keeping the work readable.

The second beat introduces the broader project context:

| Work | What the site establishes |
|---|---|
| Cabin at Kashuby | Your design, drawings, photographs and build |
| Calder Court | Practice project; your technical-design-to-handover responsibility |
| A School That Grows | Shortlisted competition; four-person team; your structure and sections |
| Kirk Street | Practice-project listing, with your personal contribution withheld until clarified |
| Teaching | Year 2 studio teaching at Clyde School of Architecture |

Visitors can open project records and inspect full-size imagery. Initially, practice and competition entries use factual text records; approved visual material can follow.

Approximate length: one and three-quarter screens.

**5. Details — close inspection**

One genuine cabin timber detail becomes the focus, accompanied by photographs that actually correspond to it.

A single sheet advances toward the visitor while the related photographic sheets remain alongside it. The movement brings the drawing into view; inspection happens through deliberate controls.

Your workshop and timber-book influences return here, connected to your interest in construction. The book is mentioned in words. Its pages are not reproduced.

Visitors can:

- Open and zoom the detail.
- Reset the view.
- Move between related photographs or another supported detail.

Joint names, drawing scales and technical explanations appear only where the material supports them.

Approximate length: one and a quarter screens.

**6. Schedules — clear scope and the next conversation**

The sheets return to a complete, aligned set. The visible top sheet carries a project-and-contribution schedule.

This is the concluding view: what you own, what you contributed to, and where each project belongs. Credits sit beside the relevant work, with a consolidated credit list below.

The close answers the opening question through the evidence already shown: your own design and construction work, and your professional responsibility for detailing, site work and handover.

Two contact routes serve your intended audience:

- An old-house or small-plot conversation.
- A guest-critic invitation.

Both can use the same supplied email address with different suggested subjects. The address is also visible and selectable. An updated CV is available here once supplied.

The object holds quietly at the end; reaching contact does not require completing another animation.

Approximate length: one and a half screens.

**Navigation and interaction**

The desktop experience is roughly nine-and-a-half viewport heights, adjusted once the real material is available. Visitors control its pace through ordinary scrolling.

A persistent chapter rail shows the six drawing-set names and the current chapter. Links jump directly to a readable state. Scrolling backwards reverses the scene naturally.

Every inspectable image has a visible HTML button such as “View drawing.” Visitors never need to discover a clickable surface in 3D.

Image viewers provide close, zoom/reset and previous/next controls where useful. They support keyboard operation and return focus to the opening control. Project records expand inline without taking visitors away from the page.

The first screen and persistent contact link serve someone with thirty seconds. No visitor needs to complete the story to find your work or reach you.

**The look**

The selected palette comes from drawing paper and ink:

| Element | Selected treatment |
|---|---|
| Ground | Warm ivory `#F2EEE5` |
| Main ink | Charcoal `#242824` |
| Accent | Oxide `#8D432D` |
| 3D sheets | Matte warm paper, crisp lines, restrained shadows |
| Photography | Large, clearly labelled images with visible credits |

The composition uses generous margins, fine rules and a consistent drawing grid. Timber’s texture comes primarily from your photographs.

**Source Sans 3** handles headings and body text. **IBM Plex Mono** handles drawing numbers, dates, scales and schedule labels. Body text starts around 18–20px on desktop and at least 16px on phones.

Two alternatives remain documented: cool tracing paper with a muted green accent, and pale sheets against a dark workshop-board ground. Warm paper is the selected direction; the site does not need a theme chooser.

**On a phone**

The same six chapters become a normal vertical document:

- One readable drawing or photograph at a time.
- Text beneath the evidence.
- Paired comparisons stacked with clear labels.
- A compact chapter menu and accessible contact link.
- Full-size drawing inspection through touch and keyboard controls.

There is no long pinned scene. A brief, shallow sheet treatment can be included if device performance supports it, but the complete experience works through the images and their relationships.

Controls have generous touch targets. Essential information never depends on hover, sideways scrolling or reading tiny annotations inside an animation.

**Without the 3D**

| Situation | Experience |
|---|---|
| Reduced motion | Static chapter arrangements; no automatic rotation, parallax or zoom. Visitors can still deliberately inspect images. |
| No WebGL or weak device | Responsive drawings and photographs, with explicit comparison labels and a static drawing-set composition. |
| No JavaScript | Complete HTML chapters, images, project records, credits, anchor navigation and email links. Full-size drawings open as ordinary files. |

All essential text and controls exist outside the scene. The animation enhances the relationships between evidence; it does not contain the only copy of the evidence.

**Everything else the site needs**

“Initial” below means part of a future implementation, not an instruction to build now.

| Requirement | Scope |
|---|---|
| Chapter navigation | Initial: anchors, active chapter indicator, skip links and shareable section addresses |
| Project index | Initial: all supplied projects, with accurate practice/team attribution |
| Individual project pages | Later, when assets and contribution records support fuller case studies |
| Contact | Initial: supplied email, visible address and two inquiry routes |
| CV | Initial once updated; replace the old title |
| Credits and permissions | Initial: per-image credits, project ownership and an asset permission register |
| Testimonials | Later, only with actual quotes and permission |
| Languages | English initially; Polish later if you want it |
| Search visibility | Descriptive titles, metadata, crawlable content, canonical address and sitemap |
| Shared-link preview | Owned cabin image or drawing with your name and work descriptor |
| Site icon | Original drawing-sheet mark |
| Missing-page handling | Helpful 404 with home and contact links |
| Accessibility | Semantic content, keyboard navigation, focus states, drawing descriptions and reduced motion; WCAG 2.2 AA target |
| Performance | Responsive images, delayed loading of later imagery, simple sheet geometry and idle rendering pauses |
| Privacy/legal information | Appropriate to the actual owner, hosting and data collection chosen before launch |
| Analytics/contact form | Later if there is a clear need |
| Blog | Later when there is writing to publish |
| Chat | Outside this scope |
| Domain and hosting | Choose before implementation and launch; static or server-rendered delivery suits the fallback requirements |
| Existing website | Establish whether one exists before planning replacement or redirects |
| Maintenance | One project/asset register keeps roles, credits, imagery and scene labels consistent |

**Assumptions and content boundaries**

I chose English first, email contact, warm paper, six editorial sheets and an image-led phone experience. Your future practice is an ambition, not presented as an operating business today.

The 68% heating-demand figure stays outside the main sequence until its baseline is available. Any later inclusion must identify it as modelled, attribute it appropriately and state that in-use measurement has not yet occurred.

Actual image selection remains pending. Missing drawings will be handled with genuine related evidence and clear labels. The time-lapse, book reproductions, third-party imagery and photographs of other people are outside the initial asset dependencies.

This completes the planning deliverable. Final captions and asset selections remain future work; no website, prototype or deployment has been created.
